2320: You watched the doors slide open and shut, letting strangers out in polite little batches. Yours next.
2321: A child in the greeting crowd waved at every single person who came through the doors, just in case.
2322: You looked up at the giant board of signs, chose the friendliest arrow, and trusted it with your afternoon.
2323: The crowd carried its bags and its excitement toward the exit. You carried a suitcase and a hunch.
2324: Someone's sign had a heart drawn on it. You weren't the traveler it was for, but it cheered you up anyway.
2325: You reached the exit doors and paused, letting a whole loud family reunion pass before you slipped out.
2326: You stood at the edge of the greeting crowd, scanning faces, which is your job exactly, minus the hugging.
2327: Every arrow led to a bigger room with more arrows. You began to suspect the building was enjoying this.
2328: The crowd flowed past the greeters and, being made of people, kept stopping to hug and block everyone behind.
2329: You walked beneath a long ribbon of signs, reading each one in your head to feel a little more in control.
2330: Everyone at the barrier held up a phone, filming a reunion that had not started yet, just to be safe.
2331: You followed one sign to the next to the next, trusting a chain of arrows drawn by people you'll never thank.
2332: The doors parted, the waiting crowd leaned in as one, saw it wasn't theirs, and gently leaned back again.
2333: You slipped through the exit with the crowd, entirely unnoticed, which for once was exactly the plan.
2334: A sign pointed hopefully at the ceiling, as if your answer were somewhere up among the bright lights.
2335: The arrivals hall had chairs, plants, and a thousand hellos and goodbyes all at the very same volume.
2336: You looked for a familiar face out of pure habit, found a hall full of strangers, and pressed on cheerfully.
2337: Someone held up a sign with just a smiling face drawn on it, trusting their traveler would simply know.
2338: The crowd at the barrier parted to let each arrival find their people. You, meanwhile, found the exit.
2339: You picked a sign, committed to it completely, and only much later wondered if it had meant something else.
2340: A pair of grandparents watched the doors so intently you almost wished their traveler could be you.
2341: The exit doors were the one sign the whole hall agreed on. You joined the agreement and stepped through.
2342: You threaded through the greeting crowd like a polite ghost, present, unmet, and perfectly on schedule.
2343: The overhead signs cycled through language after language, offering the same unhelpful thing in each one, fairly.
2344: You reached the wide empty middle of the arrivals hall, where a long trip finally sets you down and wanders off.
2345: A little group by the doors held balloons for someone. Not you, but you admired the whole effort sincerely.
2346: You joined the crowd because it was clearly going somewhere, and going somewhere was, broadly, your entire plan.
2347: The greeting crowd held signs, phones, and flowers, a small forest of welcome you politely walked past.
2348: You slid into the crowd and matched its pace exactly, briefly indistinguishable from someone who knew the way.
2349: The officer held your passport photo up beside your actual face and weighed the resemblance with visible doubt.
2350: "Anything to declare?" Only that you're extremely tired and mildly heroic. You declared neither one.
2351: The officer asked who you were visiting. You had no name yet, only a strong and quiet professional interest.
2352: You practiced looking innocent in the queue, which is exactly what a guilty person would practice. Relax.
2353: The stamp came down with a firm thud, and some small part of you felt officially real again.
2354: The officer asked the purpose of your visit. "Justice," you thought. "Tourism," you said. Simpler.
2355: You handed over your passport and your entire face, and the officer compared the two at their own leisure.
2356: The line to the passport booth moved with the quiet urgency of a very patient glacier. You waited anyway.
2357: "Business or pleasure?" A fair question you have never once managed to answer honestly. Pleasure, then.
2358: The officer flipped slowly through your passport, admiring your travels like a small, dull photo album.
2359: You stood behind the yellow line, exactly as instructed, feeling like the most obedient person alive.
